Ah, the Classic Oxford. Long may it reign.
While this "every guy" staple is technically distinguished by its collar buttons, the shirt owes its decades-long popularity among everyone from preps, to rude boys, to mods and millennials, to its enduringly simple and classic design. The shirts are meant to be the solid "fail-safe" option when you waver between dressing up or dressing down. Our Eagle Creek is sensible enough not to mess with a good thing, but it does include a few thoughtful improvements to the traditional wear experience: weve swapped the sometimes stuffy oxford cloth of old for a tightly woven, sanforized cotton fabric that will retain its shape and size, and weve pre-broken the garment with a vigorous sand wash to give it our signature weathered hand. Better yet, with every wash and every wear, the shirt builds character. Like your favorite jeans. This is one looker thatll always be a pleasure to wear, and is guaranteed to never go out of style.

The so-called “Ivy” style began with students at American East Coast colleges experimenting with sportier, dressed-down versions of gentlemanly British wardrobes. A perfect example is the unstructured suit jacket, which takes the sturdy fabrics and classic silhouettes of a British sports coat and makes it more casual with light construction and no shoulder pads. Kamakura Shirts’ version of this jacket is based on the preferred style of university students in the Fifties, coming in English gray herringbone wool tweed from Abraham Moon & Sons or a Japanese navy corduroy. Both can be dressed up with proper slacks and a necktie or dressed down with jeans. All of the details are pure Ivy: natural shoulders, a narrow three-inch lapel, a three-roll-two front closure, no front darts, a patch pocket on the chest, patch-and-flap side pockets, and a center hook vent at back.
